subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Expansion Joints: Letting Bridges Breathe
description: One-minute skill: Expansion Joints: Letting Bridges Breathe.

hook.text: On a hot day, the Golden Gate Bridge is 40 centimeters longer than on a cold day.

buildup.text: Steel expands when heated and contracts when cooled. A 300-meter bridge can grow half a meter in summer.

discovery.text: Expansion joints are intentional gaps in the bridge deck. They let sections slide without cracking.

twist.text: The bump you feel driving onto a bridge? That's the expansion joint. Without it, the road would buckle.

climax.text: Engineers use finger joints, sliding plates, and rubber seals to handle movement while keeping the road smooth.

punchline.text: Bridges grow and shrink. Engineers plan for it.

quiz.question: Why do bridges need expansion joints?
options: To reduce the total weight of the bridge structure
To allow steel to expand and contract with temperature changes
To make the bridge easier to disassemble for repairs
